# Finiteness of semigroups generated by bi-reversible invertible automata is undecidable

Finiteness of the semigroup generated by an automaton remains undecidable when the input automaton is required to be bi-reversible and bi-deterministic (but not necessarily complete), and so does the existence of an infinite orbit on infinite words.

Let $\mathcal{T} = (Q, \Sigma, \delta)$ range over [automata](automaton-semigroups.md) that are bi-reversible and bi-deterministic; such an automaton need not be complete, so its states act by partial maps and $\mathscr{S}(\mathcal{T})$ is a semigroup of partial maps on $\Sigma^*$. For $\xi \in \Sigma^\omega$, its orbit is $Q^* \circ \xi$, the set of images of $\xi$ under all products of states for which they are defined.

**Theorem (D'Angeli, Rodaro and Wächter).** The following problems are undecidable (Theorem 4.7 of arXiv:1712.07408v3):

1. given a bi-reversible and bi-deterministic automaton $\mathcal{T}$, is $\mathscr{S}(\mathcal{T})$ finite? In particular it is undecidable whether an automaton subsemigroup of an automaton-inverse semigroup is finite;
2. given a bi-reversible and bi-deterministic automaton $\mathcal{T} = (Q, \Sigma, \delta)$, is there an $\omega$-word $\xi \in \Sigma^\omega$ whose orbit $Q^* \circ \xi$ is infinite?

This strengthens [the undecidability of finiteness for automaton semigroups](finiteness-of-automaton-semigroups-undecidable.md) toward automaton groups, whose finiteness problem the source records as open. An automaton-inverse semigroup is the inverse semigroup generated by the states of an inverse-deterministic automaton and of its inverse.

## Expansion

The source first characterizes finiteness of $\mathscr{S}(\mathcal{T})$ through the dynamics on $\Sigma^\omega$: for these automata the semigroup is infinite exactly when some $\omega$-word has an infinite orbit (Section 4 of arXiv:1712.07408v3). It then reduces from Lukkarila's theorem that the tiling problem for Wang tiles remains undecidable for 4-way deterministic aperiodic tile sets, building from such a tile set a bi-reversible and bi-deterministic automaton in the spirit of Gillibert's construction. A good expansion links Lukkarila's theorem on 4-way deterministic tile sets, which has no page.

The erratum included in that version concerns the freeness results of Section 3 and does not affect Theorem 4.7.
